reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown concede Jeconiah was actually Josiah's grandson, explaining that Matthew's genealogy skips Jehoiakim as an inconsequential vassal king.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg lines up the two genealogies and finds Matthew's begat-chain makes Josiah the father, not the grandfather, of Jechonias.

quotes.text: Matthew: “Josias begat Jechonias” ( i, 11 ). Josias was not the father but the grandfather of Jechonias. “And the sons of Josiah were, ... the second Jehoiakim.... And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jechoniah, his son” ( 1 Chron. iii, 15, 16 ).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on 1 Chronicles 3:16 and Matthew 1:11.

sides.snippet: The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son
sides.verseText: The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.

sides.snippet: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers
sides.verseText: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
